primaryGoal: Avoid prolonged unresponsive startup without requiring a height cache

measureDefinitions.openToRowsMs: Host Reader.open call to native rows observed after initialization
measureDefinitions.firstFrameMs: Reader factory to first row animation-frame callback
measureDefinitions.firstNativeContentFrameMs: Reader factory to a frame opportunity with a non-placeholder native row intersecting the viewport; not Markdown completion
measureDefinitions.maxTimerGapMs: Maximum 16ms interval gap during the startup observation window

limitations: One enabled baseline aborted the attempted six-run alternating comparison
Earlier 120-second debugger timeouts were confounded by geometry/cache collection and are not user-hang durations
Current candidate still has roughly 0.6-second startup timer gaps
API selection and focus checks do not establish mouse/touch/editing compatibility
Top-start viewport assumption; restored scroll positions and other document types require further validation
The current native-row runtime was active and cached 423 rows with 411 deferred previews: placeholder height invalidation and filter relaxation remain unverified
One current-build full-preview baseline completed with a 2920ms timer gap; the earlier prolonged failure is not a claim that every current-build open persistently hangs

nativeProfiler.interpretation: Both full-preview runs have a roughly 140-160 second main-thread task dominated by native platform accessibility show/hide notifications. The same sample with progressive previews has a maximum profiled task near 403 ms. This establishes one native blocking path, not the cause of every large-document hang.
caveats: Marker intervals are wall time, may nest, and must not be added across names as exclusive CPU costs.
One profiled run per condition; sequential same-process runs and profiler overhead do not establish a population effect or incidence.
Addon-disabled means the Annotation Markdown add-on itself was disabled, with native-row and Markdown settings also disabled; the development MCP bridge remained active.
The external UI Automation instantiator was identified locally, but its application name/path is omitted from public evidence. Activation does not prove responsibility for the delay.
Progressive startup retains 411 preview placeholders and does not measure full-list materialization or long scroll sessions.
Raw native profiles and private metadata remain under ignored .tmp only.

navigationRegression.fix: New single selection gets bounded viewport correction; manual wheel/pointer/touch/keyboard input cancels it.

caveats: Three sequential visible window runs and one native tab lifecycle run on the same 423-annotation sample, not universal performance or failure-incidence claims.
Window runs use the baseline measurement probe only; native startup deferral comes from the installed production package.
Tab run uses native opening without the isolated prototype probe.
API selection/focus, DOM click, middle scrolling, tag filtering and live preference disable do not cover all real editing gestures or host versions.
Remaining maximum startup timer gaps are about 0.39-0.66 seconds; input responsiveness is not completely smooth.
Factory eager viewport size remains an estimate; native restored positions, widths/fonts/images and larger samples still merit manual validation.

limitations: Sequential samples from one 423-annotation PDF; earlier eager reference followed an app restart, so cache warming prevents a general speedup claim.
The gate requires primary-view initialization, successful current-page visible canvas rendering, and two animation-frame opportunities; this is not OS pixel presentation evidence.
The independent canvas probe can precede restored-view initialization; runtime bodyFrameMs is the stronger acceptance gate.
A ten-second timeout opens progressive recovery; explicit user intent can load an individual preview earlier.
One invalid harness attempt captured an old opening method before enabling the new preference and bypassed the patch; it is excluded from performance data.

automaticRestore.timingMeaning: Process-start to Annotation Markdown startup log, not a measured PDF first-frame or exact unresponsive interval.

limitations: One manual reopen with the normal active plugin set. Not an alternating A/B benchmark and not a root-cause profile.
The main window was restored to normal size (927x594), so timings do not represent the user maximized window.
The visible current page was 35; the copied development document did not establish identical restored position and plugin environment.
PDF frame timing is a canvas completion and animation-frame opportunity observation. A later screenshot verified visible content.
Accessibility was false at the final readback; the prior accessibility profile cannot be assigned as the cause of this run.

cleanup.note: The successful preference-restore response reported all four user values cleared; disk preferences and the closed listener were checked separately. Clearing remote-enabled closed the debug connection before removal of the inert collector result object; it contains only aggregate metrics and disappears with the window.

dailyProfileRetest.decision: The current package does not meet the daily-profile startup goal. Cover automatic restore before Reader creation, revisit the ten-second fallback while PDF loading continues, and profile the actual daily opening path before claiming success.

changes: Defer a selected large Zotero 10 Reader tab in serialized native session selection until startup hooks are installed; retain all tabs and native reading-position storage.
Keep supported PDF loading/visibility deferred after ten seconds, with progressive fallback on failed/unsupported probes and rejected loading tasks.
limitations: Development and interim daily restart tests used the interim hash. The final hash additionally catches loading-task failures and was verified installed and manually reopened in the daily profile.
Sequential normal-window runs with warm caches and hot add-on reloads are not a randomized A/B comparison or a general speedup claim.

A current-page canvas/frame probe can precede completion of restored-position initialization. Strict runtime pdf-painted readiness and final view state validate ordering; early frame timings do not denote full readiness.
Both Weavero and Ethereal Style were disabled together for one reversible hot-isolation sample. It cannot identify individual causal costs. Both are restored.

The profiled cold sample stopped before strict body readiness. Its initial false comment check arose from null/empty-string API normalization; a normalized readback verified no comment changes. Raw profiles are private ignored files.

The final reading-state comparison retained page, scale, horizontal offset and modes but differed by three PDF vertical coordinates after repeated layout/reload; pixel-exact restoration is not established.
Only selected pane Reader tabs are parked. Standalone Reader windows retain native restoration. If the add-on cannot run on the next launch, the parked book remains available as an unloaded tab.
Remaining latency and one-to-two-second timer gaps persist with the full plugin set. The overall large-document latency objective is not fully achieved.
